JobArguments.start__output__disputeDescription: Charged 14 units at $300 but the contracted unit price is $290.

outputs.rationale:
This dispute is classified under SOP §5.4 "Incorrect rate" — the customer claims the billed unit price ($300) disagrees with their contracted rate ($290) for 14 units, with quantity not in dispute. Per the SOP procedure: (1) locate the matching sowReference for the disputed line via description keyword match, (2) read the contractedRate from the ERP record for that line, (3) if unitPrice ≠ contractedRate, determination = valid with credit = (unitPrice − contractedRate) × quantity = ($300 − $290) × 14 = $140; if unitPrice = contractedRate, determination = invalid.

However, I cannot render a final valid/invalid determination because the SOP requires this check to be grounded in the ERP system-of-record data — specifically the sowReference and contractedRate fields for the disputed line on invoice MCS-2026-04872 (per SOP §4.2, ERP is "Source of truth" for sowReference, sowStatus, and contractedRate used in incorrect-rate checks). No ERP lookup tool/data was provided to this agent, and the dispute submission itself does not include a SOW reference or independently verifiable contracted rate record beyond the customer's own assertion of "$290."

The SOP also explicitly states: "Always cite the SOW reference and the rate delta... Generic rate explanations are not acceptable." Without an ERP-sourced SOW reference and contractedRate value to cite, I cannot produce a compliant valid/invalid determination — doing so would require inventing a SOW reference or accepting the customer's stated rate as ground truth, which is not permitted.

Therefore, determination is set to "needs-more-information": the underlying ERP record (sowReference and contractedRate for the disputed line on invoice MCS-2026-04872) is required before a valid/invalid call and credit calculation (potentially $140 credit at 14 units × $10/unit delta) can be issued per §5.4.
